title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: The cheap-inference window is closing on a date — Sonnet 5's promo pricing ($2/$10) ends Aug 31; standard $3/$15 hits Sep 1
bullets.summary: Anthropic confirmed Claude Sonnet 5's promotional token pricing expires at month-end (a 50% step-up on input and output) and errored out claude-opus-4-7 fast-mode, pushing migration to Opus 5 / Opus 4.8.
bullets.how: Hard, dated cost event for the whole fleet: re-baseline Ledger's routing economics now, push high-volume batch to Flash-class / cache-heavy paths before Sep 1, and lock the model-routing table so the 50% Sonnet bump doesn't quietly raise every operator's unit cost.

bullets.title: The stateless MCP spec (2026-07-28) is now shipping across the ecosystem — Agentgateway 1.4 supports it and Google published stateless-scaling guidance
bullets.summary: Within a week of the spec, gateways and clouds are moving: Agentgateway shipped 1.4 with full 2026-07-28 support (Aug 3) and Google published a stateless-scaling playbook, confirming the 'server in a single Worker, no session store' pattern is real infra now.
bullets.how: The migration path for The Construct's MCP fleet is validated in the wild; re-target internal servers at the stateless core and put an Agentgateway-class layer in front rather than hand-rolling session glue.

bullets.title: Anthropic keeps hardening the Enterprise runtime — skill/plugin security scanning + Claude Code self-hosted environments + inference-hook DLP
bullets.summary: Automatic malware scanning of third-party skills/plugins on upload/edit, public-beta self-hosted Claude Code environments (own infra, internal network, compliance controls), cross-session messaging, removal of the subagent spawn cap, and Enterprise inference hooks doing real-time DLP on prompts/tool calls before the model.
bullets.how: Governance-as-substrate for exactly what we do: gate the installed-skills registry on 'scanned + signed', move the swarm onto uncapped cross-talking subagents, and sell provable DLP + data-residency as a PRAGMA feature.

bullets.title: Frontier holds — GPT-5.6 is OpenAI's rolling default across ChatGPT/Codex/API; Gemini 4 remains in pre-training with no benchmarks, price, or date
bullets.summary: No new flagship weight in the last 24h; GPT-5.6 (88.8% Terminal-Bench 2.1, 91.9% ultra) is the freshest shipping default alongside Claude Opus 5 and stable Gemini 3.6 Flash, while Gemini 4 is unreleased.
bullets.how: Hold the cost/quality routing split and pre-wire an eval harness so we can benchmark Gemini 4 the day it drops rather than scrambling.

bullets.title: The agent-economy capital wave is a competitive signal for PRAGMA — Glean $150M Series F at $7.2B (100M+ agent actions/yr), Cognition near $25B, Perplexity $200M near $20B
bullets.summary: Horizontal 'deploy agents at scale' platforms (Glean Agents) and coding-agent shops (Cognition) are raising at agentic-platform multiples, and the surface where an agent starts and finishes a task is where the capital is going.
bullets.how: These are the incumbents PRAGMA's operator-as-plugin wedge sells against; the differentiator isn't 'we have agents' but governed, scanned, spec-defined operators packaged as a client's own function — sell the guardrails and packaging the platform players don't.

praxis_lesson: The rails are done hardening and pricing is normalizing — the stateless MCP spec is shipping in real gateways/clouds this week, Anthropic keeps adding scanning/self-hosting/DLP, and the cheap-inference window has an expiry date (Sonnet 5 promo ends Aug 31). Two moves fall out: lock the fleet's routing economics before the Sep 1 price step so margin doesn't leak, and keep building the moat one layer up from both the model and the protocol — scanned, spec-defined, portable operators whose governance is the product while weights, protocol, and now even inference price commoditize beneath.
